FN-Y84W266-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 1
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/12/2025
Senate Bill 1 as introduced would establish the Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Program to provide injury compensation benefits to full-time public K-12
education employees beginning no later than October 1, 2026.
Additionally, this bill would create the five-member Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Board to administer the program and oversee the benefits paid to injured
employees. This bill provides that members of the board shall not receive compensation but may
be reimbursed for travel and per diem expenses paid from the fund at the same rate as state
employees.
Further, this bill would establish the non-reverting Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Trust Fund in the State Treasury to fund the program. Based on information
provided by privately contracted workers' compensation consultants, the cost of this program to
provide coverage for full-time public K-12 employees would be an estimated minimum of $14.9
million.

FN-Y84W266-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 1
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 03/17/2025
Senate Bill 1 as passed the Senate would establish the Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Program to provide compensation benefits in accordance with the Alabama
Workers' Compensation Act to full-time public K-12 and post secondary education employees,
beginning no later than October 1, 2026.
Additionally, this bill would establish the non-reverting Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Trust Fund in the State Treasury to fund the program and would require
participation by all local boards of education, subject to sufficient appropriations to the fund.
Based on information provided by privately contracted workers' compensation consultants, the
start-up and first year cost of this program would be an estimated minimum of $15.6 million.
Further, this bill would create the five-member Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Board to administer the program and would provide that members of the board
not receive compensation but may be reimbursed for travel and per diem expenses paid from the
fund at the same rate as state employees.
